short: Walk length and the 1 mHa error budget

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.SevenGearWalk333.fast7gUnitProg
lean.plain: The 47,487-step phase-estimation circuit
lean.annotation: The schedule runs 45,440 steps with 160 workspace qubits, 1,024 with 159, seven blocks of 128 with 156, and 127 single steps with 149. Removing one borrowed qubit adds $2\times448=896$ $T$ across two SELECT calls. The final single steps use a different implementation to fit the smaller workspace.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.P450GroundEnergy.TopBridge.solution_fg_correctness
lean.plain: Correctness of the 47,487-step circuit
lean.annotation: The rational certificate bounds the ideal sine-window term by 0.997240 mHa. The Hamiltonian perturbation contributes 0.000400 mHa. The state error from phase-gradient preparation, window preparation and inverse QFT is at most $4.958\times10^{-8}$. Multiplication by the gap bound gives less than 0.000240 mHa. The scheduled walk blocks add zero relative to their effective walk. The total is below 0.998 mHa.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.TightGapDeep63.p450RefVarBound_tightGapDeep63
lean.plain: Variational upper bound on the cutoff
lean.annotation: The proof bounds the energy expectation of the reference state and obtains a sector eigenvalue no larger than it. Substituting this eigenvalue into $T\le E'+0.1$ gives $T\le-130.0526$ Ha. The circuit has no cutoff input.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.P450GroundEnergy.TopBridge.mainHeff_agree
lean.plain: Operator error on the 63-electron sector
lean.annotation: In `mainHeff_agree`, the outer preparation changes its probability distribution by a sum of absolute differences at most $24\times10^{-11}$. Combining this with the inner bound gives $\|P_{63}(H_{\rm eff}-H_{\rm blocked})P_{63}\|\le4\times10^{-7}$ Ha. The effective Hamiltonian also commutes with $P_{63}$.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.TailShiftBox.dh4000
lean.plain: Hamiltonian error allowance of 4 × 10⁻⁷ Ha
lean.annotation: `dh4000` names the quantization-error allowance `4000/10^10 = 4 × 10⁻⁷ Ha`. The manuscript attributes this 63-electron-sector Hamiltonian perturbation to synthesized state-preparation rotations and reports that it is included alongside phase-estimation error.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.TailShiftBox.g_deep63
lean.plain: Upper bound on the range of capped energies
lean.annotation: Both the true and decoded energies are at least the sum-of-squares lower bound. A higher cutoff puts their capped values in the interval from that lower bound to $T$, of width at most 4.834842 Ha. At a cutoff below the lower bound both capped values equal $T$.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.mse_impl_le_of_ideal_and_perturbation
lean.plain: RMS energy bound for the implemented output state
lean.annotation: `scaleVec` multiplies each output amplitude by the capped energy difference for its ancilla outcome. Its squared norm is the mean squared error. Every multiplier has magnitude at most $E_{\rm gap}$, so the triangle inequality adds at most $E_{\rm gap}\delta_W$ to the ideal RMS bound for an output-state error of norm at most $\delta_W$.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.TwoGearQPEPhase5.capped_perturbed_measuresLowEnergiesAt_box_tg
lean.plain: Phase estimation, Hamiltonian and circuit errors
lean.annotation: Expand the input eigenstate in an orthonormal basis of effective eigenvectors with coefficients $c_j$. The spread $\sum_j|c_j|^2(\tilde E_j-E)^2$ equals $\|(H_{\rm eff}-E)\psi\|_2^2\le\delta_H^2$. At each ideal outcome the branches remain orthogonal, so their probabilities add with weights $|c_j|^2$. Capping can only decrease each difference. The RMS triangle inequality adds $\delta_H$ to the ideal bound.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.P450GroundEnergy.TopBridge.fast7g_estTransferHyp
lean.plain: From spin-blocked orbitals to the fixed Hamiltonian
lean.annotation: The proof undoes the spin-blocked order by a fermionic permutation. Each fermionic swap has the extra sign on $|11\rangle$ and preserves electron number. The permutation acts on the system alone, leaving the phase probabilities unchanged. Embedding the active ancillas and extracting the same bits preserves the estimate.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.P450GroundEnergy.TopBridge.solution_fg_correctness
lean.plain: Correctness of the 47,487-step circuit
lean.annotation: The ideal sine window has support on indices 0 through $M=47{,}487$ of the 16-bit phase register. The forward and backward schedule applies $U^{2m-M}$ at supported index $m$. On an eigenstate of walk phase $\varphi$, this gives phase $2m\varphi$ up to a factor common to the supported indices. The inverse QFT estimates the doubled phase.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.TightGapDeep63.p450RefVarBound_tightGapDeep63
lean.plain: Variational upper bound on the cutoff
lean.annotation: For any cutoff `T` at most 0.1 Ha above every eigenvalue in the 63-electron sector, the variational certificate gives `T ≤ −130.0526 Ha` without identifying the ground state. The manuscript uses this reference to tighten the gap measured from the sum-of-squares lower bound and reduce the walk length.
